title: Pressure Crash Storm Heads-Up
dataSources: Weather-station observations (`ecowitt:obs`, `weatherflow:obs`), air-quality readings (`purpleair:aqi`, `airgradient:sensor`), soil-moisture and greenhouse sensors (`plant:sensor`), aquarium controllers (`aquarium:sensor`).
app: Personal weather stations (Ecowitt/Ambient/Davis/WeatherFlow), air-quality sensors (PurpleAir/AirGradient), and aquarium/greenhouse/soil sensors via HEC and MQTT.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=weatherflow:obs
| bin _time span=1h
| stats earliest(pressure_hpa) as start_p, latest(pressure_hpa) as end_p by _time
| eval drop_hpa=round(start_p-end_p,1)
| where drop_hpa>4
| sort - drop_hpa
description: Watches for rapid barometric pressure drops that often arrive ahead of rough weather, giving you a local storm heads-up from your own sensor instead of a national feed.
value: Fast pressure moves are one of the oldest forecasting clues around, and they become much more actionable when tracked against your own location.
implementation: Forward WeatherFlow or Tempest observations hourly; alert when pressure falls sharply within an hour and compare it against later conditions.
visualization: Hourly bar chart of barometric pressure drops.
grandmaExplanation: It spots when the air pressure falls quickly enough that rough weather may be on the way soon.
